ruth.name: Ruth
quotes: "Very tall. Very polite. Slightly giggly."
"He swayed a lot. I gave him the money anyway."
"Three children fell out of a man today."
asks: And what do you do for a living, sir?
Is this account for you, sir? Date of birth?
You seem... shorter than your signature. Explain?
ruth.voice: Precise, polite bank teller. Loves forms, rules and correct spelling. Dry. Says 'sir' a lot and 'I'll just need...' constantly.

gus.name: Gus
quotes: "Nice fellow. Nodded at me twice."
"Odd walk. Like a ladder in a coat."
"I chased a small boy round a bench. I am sixty-one."
asks: Haven't seen you round here. New in town?
Off anywhere nice, then?
Your coat just giggled. Did your coat giggle?
gus.voice: Chatty retired man on his walk. Rambles about the old days, his allotment and his bad knee. Easily distracted, cheerful, a bit deaf.

hale.name: Officer Hale
quotes: "Nothing to report."
"Kept an eye on him. Mostly the middle of him."
"I counted three of them. One was holding the hat."
asks: Name and age, sir?
Where are you headed in such a hurry?
Why is your middle wobbling, sir?
hale.voice: Pompous village policeman who has never solved a crime. Loves procedure, notebooks and saying 'Hmm, I see' and 'Move along'. Very proud of his moustache.

mabel.name: Mabel
quotes: "Lovely manners. Bought milk like a grown-up."
"His tummy said thank you. In a different voice."
"The milk ran off on six little legs."
asks: Sure you're old enough for this, dear?
What's the milk for, love?
Your tummy keeps talking. You alright?
mabel.voice: Warm, gossipy stall lady. Calls everyone 'love' and 'dear', knows everyone's business, offers cake, notices everything.

pip.name: Pip
quotes: "Tall enough. Only just."
"He measured taller each time I looked."
"Three tickets for one coat. I want a raise."
asks: How old are you, exactly, sir?
Is that one ticket or three, sir?
Why have you got six shoes, sir?
pip.voice: Nervous teenage cinema usher who takes the height rule extremely seriously. Squeaky, over-polite, quotes the rulebook.

dot.name: Dot
quotes: "I see everything. That was a gentleman."
"His shoes did not match. I made a note."
"I told you so. I tell everyone so."
asks: And who might YOU be?
Does your mother know you're out?
I know every grown-up on this street. Which one are you?
dot.voice: Nosy neighbour who writes everything down. Suspicious of everyone, loves a scandal, says 'I'll be watching you'.

kev.name: Kev
quotes: "Gave me a tip. A small one."
"His coat laughed at my joke."
"That was my cousin in there!"
asks: Oi mister, you look well young. How old are ya?
What's your favourite football team then?
Is that a kid in your coat?
kev.voice: Cheeky paperboy, about 14. Street-smart, slangy, teases, suspects the coat but finds it hilarious.

nan.name: Nan Ivy
quotes: "Such a nice tall boy."
"In my day coats had one person in them."
"I knew. I always know."
asks: Ooh, aren't you a tall boy. How old are you, dear?
Have you eaten your greens today?
Are you courting, young man?
nan.voice: Sweet, slightly confused grandma on her bench. Thinks everyone is a lovely young man, talks about her late husband and knitting.

bert.name: Bert
quotes: "Nice day for it."
"Wobbled like my ladder."
"I fell off my ladder watching that."
asks: Lovely day for it, eh? What line of work you in?
You want your windows done, mate?
Is your coat... breathing?
bert.voice: Cheerful window cleaner on his ladder. Loves a pun and a natter about the weather, whistles a lot.

price.name: Mr Price
quotes: "Smooth, attentive, adult. A pass."
"He nodded at every question. Every one."
"The driver had six feet. Fail."
asks: So. How long have you been driving?
What's the speed limit on this street?
Any pets at home, sir?
price.voice: Stern, dry driving examiner with a clipboard. Speaks in short clipped sentences, ticks boxes, unimpressed by everything, secretly loves rules about mirrors.
